sources.title: Azure Well-Architected Framework - Design review checklist for Cost Optimization

waf.title: Create a culture of financial responsibility
waf.recommendation: Regularly train personnel so technical skills stay sharp. Foster creativity and spending accountability, and invest in tooling and automation.

waf.title: Create and maintain a cost model
waf.recommendation: Estimate initial cost, run rates and ongoing costs. Negotiate a budget that covers the cost model and has a buffer for unplanned spending.

waf.title: Collect and review cost data
waf.recommendation: Capture daily costs. Include metered and amortized costs, trends and forecasts. Review spending against budget, and automate alerts and anomaly detection.

waf.title: Set spending guardrails
waf.recommendation: Use release gates, governance policies, resource limits and access controls. Prefer platform automation over manual processes.

waf.title: Get the best rates from providers
waf.recommendation: Find and use the best rates for resources and licenses. Review regional pricing, pricing tiers, consumption versus commitment models, license portability and price sheets.

waf.title: Align usage to billing increments
waf.recommendation: Understand billing meters and align resource usage to those increments, modifying the service or the usage pattern to fit.

waf.title: Optimize component costs
waf.recommendation: Regularly remove or optimize legacy, unneeded and underutilized workload components, including application features, platform features and resources.

waf.title: Optimize environment costs
waf.recommendation: Prioritize spending across preproduction, production, operations and disaster recovery. Consider availability, licensing, operating hours and security per environment, and apply strategic tradeoffs in nonproduction.

waf.title: Optimize flow costs
waf.recommendation: Align the cost of each flow with the priority of that flow, considering features, functionality and nonfunctional requirements.

waf.title: Optimize data costs
waf.recommendation: Align data spending with data priority. Improve tiering and retention, volume, replication, backups, file formats and storage choices.

waf.title: Optimize code costs
waf.recommendation: Evaluate and modify code so it meets functional and nonfunctional requirements with fewer or cheaper resources.

waf.title: Optimize scaling costs
waf.recommendation: Evaluate alternative scaling configurations within scale units, align them with the cost model, and use strategies that control both demand and supply.

waf.title: Optimize personnel time
waf.recommendation: Align time spent with task priority. Reduce noise, build times and debugging effort without degrading outcomes.

waf.title: Consolidate resources and responsibility
waf.recommendation: Consolidate resources and increase density inside the workload, and use existing centralized services outside it.

finops.title: Deliver cost visibility and shared accountability
finops.practice: Allocate cost to owners, benchmark, budget and forecast so every team can see what it spends before it is asked to change anything.

finops.title: Reduce waste and improve efficiency
finops.practice: Apply workload optimization such as rightsizing and scheduling, then rate optimization such as reservations and savings plans. Usage changes first, rate commitments second.

finops.title: Govern continuously against business goals
finops.practice: Define and track KPIs and governance policies, assign owners, and review on a recurring cadence so savings persist instead of drifting back.

finops.title: Architecting for the cloud
finops.practice: Choose services and topologies that match demand, favouring elastic and serverless options where the workload is bursty or idle for long periods.

finops.title: Workload optimization
finops.practice: Rightsize to observed utilization, shut down or scale idle non-production workloads outside working hours, and remove orphaned resources.

finops.title: Rate optimization
finops.practice: Commit to reservations or savings plans only for steady, predictable baseline usage, after usage has been optimized, and track utilization of what you commit to.

finops.title: Anomaly management
finops.practice: Detect deviations from the trend baseline quickly and route them to an owner, because unexplained spikes are usually the cheapest savings to recover.

finops.title: Unit economics
finops.practice: Express cost per business unit such as cost per tenant or per transaction, so spending growth can be judged against value delivered rather than in absolute terms.
